value.body: An administrative executive keeps an office running: facilities and housekeeping, vendor contracts, supplies, records, travel bookings and support for meetings and events. Companies of every size hire them, as do schools, hospitals, NGOs and colleges. A typical day mixes coordination, paperwork and fixing small problems as they come up.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Any graduate — BA, B.Com or BBA

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Excel, Word, email, basic purchase or expense software

items.label: Active companies (MCA)
items.note: Companies with active status, about 65% of all registered; every company needs some office administration
items.source: Ministry of Corporate Affairs monthly bulletin (as reported)

items.label: Registered companies (MCA)
items.note: Includes inactive and struck-off companies; excludes LLPs, schools, hospitals and NGOs
items.source: Ministry of Corporate Affairs monthly bulletin (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join as admin executives, admin assistants or office coordinators through job portals, walk-ins or referrals. Clear communication, comfort with Excel and an organised approach count heavily in selection.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Excel for trackers and expense sheets

value.title: At a glance
items: The role differs a lot by employer — from a small office to a large campus.
Common next roles: admin manager, facilities manager, or a move into operations or HR.
Much of the work is reactive, so juggling many small tasks is part of the job.
